# gh-1888 re-review (report part 2/2 — Findings 4 & 5, test-run caveat)

## Finding 4 — unbounded PBKDF2 iteration count: VERIFIED

**(a) Bound exists, enforced before KDF.** `lib/src/hub/dap_key_envelope.dart:41` `const dapKeyMaxIterations = 5000000` (doc comment 33-40 explains the boot-DoS threat model). Enforcement in `decryptChannelPriv`: lines 120-126 — `decoded['iter'] as int`, then `if (iterations < 1 || iterations > dapKeyMaxIterations) throw FormatException('dapkey1: unreasonable iteration count …')` — this precedes `_deriveKey` at line 131, so zero KDF work happens for hostile values. The `on FormatException { rethrow; }` at 142-143 keeps the specific message.

**(b) One warning, primary job proceeds, no crash.** Sole production caller chain: `DapScopedMemberships._runtimeSecret` (bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:457-468) catches `FormatException` → adds ONE `loadWarnings` entry ('dap: #<channel>: <message>; re-paste the invite …') → returns null → membership stays joined keyless and seedOverlay/runtimeEffective complete. The interactive passphrase prompt has no retry loop.

**(c) No other unbounded work.** salt/nonce/ct are `base64Url.decode`d (linear in input size, envelope itself bounded by file/env size); `ct.length < 16` check at line 130; a non-int `iter` (string/double) makes `as int` throw TypeError, caught by `on Object` (144) → single FormatException. AEAD decrypt cost is linear in ct. Remaining worst case is 5M iterations ≈ seconds of CPU at boot — bounded, attacker can't multiply it further per envelope.

**(d) Tests cover hostile values.** test/hub/dap_key_envelope_test.dart:117-131 ('iter above the max is rejected BEFORE any KDF work', builds a 1e9-iter envelope directly, asserts FormatException + <5 s), :133-138 (iter 0 rejected), :140-147 (exactly max+1 rejected). The test helper builds the envelope JSON directly so no test pays the KDF.

**Residual:** 5M iterations is still seconds of blocking KDF per hostile envelope at boot; acceptable but not free. No cap on how many distinct envelopes can be attempted, only per-envelope cost.

## Finding 5 — wrong-typed pub/priv in DAP_CHANNELS_JSON crashes parse: VERIFIED

**(a) All entry fields read tolerantly.** `lib/src/hub/dap_env_channels.dart`: `entry is! Map` skip (:74-79); `channel is! String || isEmpty` skip (:73-79, warning names the index); `hubUrl is! String || isEmpty` skip (:80-86 — note `entry['hubUrl'] ?? defaultHubUrl` keeps a wrong-typed non-null hubUrl, which then correctly fails the `is! String` test and is skipped, never guessed); `pub != null && pub is! String` skip (:89-94); `priv != null && priv is! String` skip (:95-100). The final `pub as String?` / `priv as String?` casts (:107-108) are unreachable with non-strings. The entry shape is flat — there are NO nested objects to parse, and no other fields are read from env entries (scope/joinedAt are assigned, not parsed).

**(b) Skip keeps valid entries.** Each bad entry `continue`s the loop; `memberships` accumulates only valid entries and `warnings` gets one indexed line per skip.

**(c) No TypeError can escape into union()/seedOverlay()/runtimeEffective().** Env memberships are constructed as fully-typed `DapChannelMembership` objects directly — they never pass through `DapChannelMembership.fromJson` (whose `as String?` casts remain strict but are only fed project/session records, each wrapped in per-entry `try/on Object` at bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart session loader :334-336 and the project loader's identical pattern, so even those degrade to a warning + skip). `union()`/`effective()` operate on typed objects only; `_loadGlobal` is also tolerant (`if (c is String && c.isNotEmpty)`). `_loadEnv` (fah_dap_scoped.dart:341-349) folds parser warnings into `loadWarnings`.

**(d) Tests exist.** test/hub/dap_env_channels_test.dart:67-92: 'an int priv is skipped … valid entries still join' (asserts only 'ok' joins + 1 warning containing 'priv'/'skipped') and 'a list-typed pub is skipped' (asserts empty memberships + 1 warning containing 'pub'); plus a null pub/priv-tolerated test (:93+) confirming keyless entries aren't skipped.

**Residual:** none significant found. The pre-existing top-level guards (non-JSON → one warning; non-list → one warning) are also intact.

## Test-run caveat
`dart test test/hub/...` was NOT executed — this sandbox exposes no shell/exec tool (`which dart` could not be run), so tests were verified by full reading instead. All three test files are syntactically well-formed, use the real FakeHub / real parser entry points, and assert precisely the claimed behaviors; risk that they fail at runtime is low (the only runtime dependency is the fake_hub harness used elsewhere in the suite). Recommend the parent run `dart test test/hub/hub_fabric_repository_test.dart test/hub/dap_key_envelope_test.dart test/hub/dap_env_channels_test.dart` in an environment with the Dart SDK.

## Verdicts
- Finding 3: VERIFIED (residuals: refusal is silent at send time — queue/retry only; pub==null-with-priv malformed record edge)
- Finding 4: VERIFIED
- Finding 5: VERIFIED
